critical.finding: The executed capex runs at about half of management's guide, and the table's own scenario conditions say the opposite of the numbers. Guide: FY2026 capex is 'approximately $20 billion' (call) or 'in excess of $20 billion' (10-Q). Nine-month capex was 13,014M, so Q4 2026 needs at least about 7.0B. The CFO said capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, compute, a semiconductor fab). The executed capex (maintenance_capex + growth_capex) is: stub 2026-10-27..12-31 bear 3.69B, base 2.46B, bull 1.89B; FY2027 bear 5.5B, base 10.8B, bull 12.6B; FY2028 bear 5.4B, base 11.7B, bull 15.5B. Bear growth capex is zero in 2027-2028. The base condition in table_he.md says investment keeps rising until the new products sell ('about 20bn in 2026'), and the bear condition says R&D and investment keep rising. The executed paths cut capex roughly in half (base) or by three quarters (bear). The deviation from the guide is not stated anywhere: the sales_to_capital reason mentions the 20bn but not that the paths spend about half of it. In FY2027 alone, base free cash flow is overstated by about 9B even if capex only stays at the 2026 level. That is about twice the base FY2027 after-tax operating profit (~4.7B). Holding capex at even 20B a year through 2028 would cut the fair value (38.9) by roughly 10-20%. CLAUDE.md requires forecasts to be linked to investment and funding.
